purpose: Chlorothiazide helps your body get rid of extra salt and water by making you urinate more often. It is most commonly used to treat high blood pressure and fluid buildup (swelling) caused by conditions like heart failure or kidney problems. Lowering blood pressure helps reduce your risk of strokes, heart attacks, and kidney disease.
how_it_works: Your kidneys filter your blood and decide what to keep and what to flush out as urine. Chlorothiazide tells your kidneys to release more salt and water into your urine instead of keeping it in your body. With less fluid in your blood vessels, your blood pressure goes down and swelling is reduced.
common_side_effects: You may urinate more often, especially when you first start taking it. Other common side effects include dizziness, lightheadedness, low potassium levels (which can cause muscle cramps or weakness), dry mouth, thirst, nausea, and increased sensitivity to sunlight.
warnings: This medication can lower your potassium, sodium, and magnesium levels, so your doctor may check your blood regularly. Tell your doctor if you have diabetes, gout, kidney disease, or liver problems, as this drug can affect those conditions. Avoid standing up too quickly to prevent dizziness or fainting. Do not take if you are allergic to sulfa-type drugs. Stay well hydrated, especially in hot weather.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual dose for high blood pressure is 500 mg to 1,000 mg (1 gram) taken once or twice daily by mouth. For fluid retention, doses can go up to 2,000 mg per day divided into doses. Your doctor will find the right dose for you. Always take it exactly as prescribed and try to take it in the morning to avoid nighttime trips to the bathroom.
